newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Market directionless in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Market directionless in thin talk.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was dull in thin talk on Monday with most traders staying on the sidelines searching for new direction.
Fuel oil swaps were slightly up despite the overnight weakness of crude values but the physical market was indifferent, traders said.
May swaps inched up to $99.00/$99.50, up from $98.50/$99.50 on Friday.
"The market is usually quiet on Monday and it's especially so today when there is absolutely no fresh market factors," said one trader.
Sentiment was sluggish on the SIMEX futures contract with no transactions reported in late Monday trade. Both June and July contracts were bid/offered at $97.50/$98.50.
The market was awaiting the result of a Taiwan tender, which closes on May 7, to buy two 0.5-percent, 38,000-tonne cargoes for June delivery, traders said.
Some traders said prices should be supported in coming months due to fewer cargoes from the Middle East, but they also said that they did not expect any significant price movements near term.
On Friday, the 180-cst grade was heard offered at $99.50 per tonne, compared with a $98.50 traded level last week.
